subject.title: fix: forward response-frame meta to clients

question: Should Gateway v4 accept optional top-level `res.meta` after this branch is rebased, or should response metadata use a version-gated or payload-level contract instead?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but the public response envelope currently uses a strict schema, so accepting a new top-level field is a compatibility decision maintainers should own.

options.title: Accept additive `res.meta` after rebase
options.body: Rebase the PR, keep the optional schema/model/doc/test changes, and land it as an additive v4 envelope field once checks rerun.

options.title: Version-gate the field
options.body: Require protocol/version negotiation before the server emits `res.meta` to clients that may have strict old validators.

options.title: Use payload-level metadata instead
options.body: Avoid changing the top-level envelope by moving this signal into method-specific payloads or another existing client contract.

recommendation.title: Accept additive `res.meta` after rebase
recommendation.body: Rebase the PR, keep the optional schema/model/doc/test changes, and land it as an additive v4 envelope field once checks rerun.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent Gateway/protocol refactor history point to this person across the implicated response builder, schema, shared type, and generator files.
